title: A recursively enumerable theory for an effective continuous lambda-model
formal: Does an effective model of the untyped λ-calculus in Scott’s continuous semantics have a recursively enumerable equational theory?
definitions: The equational theory of a model is the set of encoded pairs of λ-terms with equal denotations, under the source’s convention for free variables. Recursively enumerable means that a Turing machine can enumerate exactly those pairs. A continuous model interprets function abstraction and application using a reflexive object in an appropriate category of domains and continuous maps. Effectiveness is the additional computability structure defined in the source, not merely a countable presentation.

context_blocks.text: Denotational semantics assigns mathematical meanings to programs. An enumerable complete equality theory would connect those meanings to a mechanically enumerable calculus of program equations.

Berline, Manzonetto and Salibra rule out recursively enumerable order theories for their effective models and obtain stronger equational impossibility results in stable settings. The order theory and equality theory are different objects, and Scott-continuous semantics is broader than the stable settings covered by those negative theorems.

why: Locate a basic boundary between effective semantic models and effective equational reasoning.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
